title: Exactly One, At Most One and Uniqueness
quickIdea: Exactly one is 'at least one' plus 'at most one': there exists x with P(x), and every y with P(y) must equal x. Uniqueness always needs a second variable and equality.
remember: At least one: there exists x P(x).
At most one: for all x for all y ((P(x) and P(y)) implies x = y), equivalently not (there exists x there exists y (P(x) and P(y) and x is not y)).
Exactly one: there exists x (P(x) and for all y (P(y) implies y = x)).
With a two-place predicate: 'x has exactly one mother' is there exists y (mother(y, x) and for all z (mother(z, x) implies z = y)).

Writing two existentials side by side does not express uniqueness: there exists y there exists z (mother(y, x) and not mother(z, x)) is satisfied by taking z to be any non-mother, so it says nothing about how many mothers x has.
When the language has no equality symbol, GATE supplies a noteq predicate; not noteq(z, y) then plays the role of z = y.
'Everyone has exactly one mother' is the uniqueness pattern inside a universal over people: for all x, the exactly-one formula for x.

example.prompt: Write 'every student has exactly one roll number', with roll(r, s): r is the roll number of s.
example.work: Outer universal over students; inside, one witness r with roll(r, s), and every other roll number of s must be that same r.
example.answer: For all s there exists r (roll(r, s) and for all t (roll(t, s) implies t = r)).

gateAngle: GATE CS 2025 Set 1 Q.38 gives four formulas for 'everyone has exactly one mother' and the correct ones are the two that pair the witness with a universal forcing every other candidate to be that witness.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: See GATE CS 2025 Set 1 Q.38 in the linked PYQs.
variations.why: Both say: there is a mother y of x, and any z that is a mother of x is y. The other options either force two different people or do not exclude a second mother.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Write 'at most one person is a ruler', with ruler(x).
variations.answer: For all x for all y ((ruler(x) and ruler(y)) implies x = y).
variations.why: At most one allows zero; the formula forbids two distinct rulers without asserting that one exists.

trap.what: Using two existentials to express uniqueness.
trap.why: Two existentials can be witnessed by unrelated elements; uniqueness needs a universal that forces every candidate to coincide with the witness.
trap.counterexample: Domain {a, b, c} with mother only a of x. There exists y there exists z (mother(y, x) and not mother(z, x)) is true with y = a and z = b, yet there is exactly one mother; the formula does not capture the count at all.

check.question: Write 'there is exactly one prime number' over the integers, with prime(x).
check.answer: There exists x (prime(x) and for all y (prime(y) implies y = x)).
check.explanation: The witness is the prime; the universal forces every prime to be that same element. (The sentence is in fact false over the integers, which is a separate matter.)
